messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts on /v1/generate in us-west-2. 5xx spike to ~20% over 3m, p95 latency spiking. Auto-pager invoked.

Anika: I'm on it. Checking schedulers and ingress. Seeing unusually high batching queue depth on scheduler-cluster-usw2; several pods showing excessive kv cache growth.

Maya: initial read looks like head-of-line caused by a handful of very large batches and tokenization CPU choking tokenizer-workers. Might be a model loader prefetch.

Tom: If that's the case, evicting the longest processing requests should free the queue quickly. Evictions will surface errors though.

Anika: Agreed. Steps I'm doing now:
- enable rate-limit for free/oss tier at the gateway
- reduce max_batch_size for high-load scheduler pods to 32
- evict 3 longest requests

Tom: I'll run the evict command. Running:
```
redwoodctl scheduler evict --cluster=usw2-scheduler --count=3 --reason="hot-batch hol mitigation"
# evicted: rq_a1c2, rq_b3d4, rq_e5f6
```

Anika: applied ingress rule:
```
redwoodctl ingress set --service=gateway --tier=public --limit=8rps
```
Incoming qps down ~28%.

Jeff: Support seeing ~15 customers reporting 502/timeouts across embeddings/chat. Mostly non-enterprise. I'm prepping a cautious status email.

Maya: logs show spikes in kv_cache_size on pods scheduler-09 and scheduler-11. Example:
```
2026-04-01T15:42:10Z pod=scheduler-09 kv_cache=2.1GB -> 5.8GB event=prefetch
2026-04-01T15:42:57Z pod=scheduler-11 long_batch_id=rq_b3d4 tokens=38000 status=processing
```

Anika: tokenizer workers CPU at 95% on a few nodes; that's propagating delay into scheduler queue.

Tom: Can we short-circuit very long inputs at the gateway for public tiers? Return a 413-like response suggesting chunking or dedicated lanes.

Anika: Patching route to reject seq_len > 16000 for public routes and direct them to dedicated if available.
```
redwoodctl routes update --path=/v1/generate --filter=seq_len<=16000 --public_action=reject
```
Patch applied.

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: after evictions + throttles p95 latency down and 5xx now ~6% over last 2m.

Tom: Diving deeper. I see a recent runtime loader change toggled `prefetch_on_hotload=true` for certain model variants. That would explain the aggressive KV prefetch and memory growth.

Tom: Temporarily disabling the runtime prefetch flag on the cluster:
```
redwoodctl runtime feature-toggle prefetch_on_hotload=false --scope=cluster:usw2
# toggled on 2 nodes
```

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: 5xx down to ~2.5%, queue depth back to normal within 5 minutes. p95 ~720ms.

Maya: recommend we add a scheduler safety that triggers auto-eviction when kv_cache growth rate > X MB/s, and alert if tokenization CPU > 80% for >1m.

Tom: I'll open an eng-ml ticket regarding the loader change and request a rollback or fix. Also adding a canary for loader flags.

Jeff: Sent customer note to affected accounts with ETA. Will update in 30m.

Lia: please include affected account IDs and whether paid tiers saw impact. I want the PM summary for customer comms.

Anika: handing off incident ownership to Tom. I'm stepping out. Tom, please coordinate the full postmortem and tag Product and Eng-ML.

Tom: Taking ownership. Summary I'm logging:
- root cause: runtime loader prefetched KV unexpectedly on some variants
- impact: head-of-line batching saturation -> timeouts and 5xx on generation endpoints
- mitigations: evict long requests, ingress rate limit, route seq_len short-circuit, disable prefetch flag
- follow-ups: revert/fix loader change, add prefetch canary, add kv growth alarms, add scheduler auto-evict threshold

incident-bot: STATUS -> mitigated. Owner=Tom. Incident doc created: https://redwood.docs/incidents/1769999999

Anika: please capture cost impact from autoscaled memory/disk in the postmortem. Also include the list Jeff shared.

Tom: Will include cost delta and customer list. Closing live page; will keep monitoring and reopen if regressions appear. :thumbsup:
